newsitem.title: UK: Monthly review - Kabila wins power in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Monthly review - Kabila wins power in Zaire.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila seized power in Zaire in May, ousting veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko with a lightning guerrilla campaign across the vast Central African state. He renamed the country the Democratic Republic of Congo. Russia and NATO signed a landmark deal on a new partnership for security in Europe and President Boris Yeltsin promised that Russian nuclear weapons would no longer be targeted at alliance countries.

Tony Blair's Labour Party swept to a landslide victory in the May 1 British general election, ending 18 years of Conservative rule. In France, left-wing opposition parties took a surprise lead in the first round of parliamentary elections.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
May 1 - Landslide election victory sweeps Tony Blair's Labour Party into power in Britain; the next day John Major announces he will resign as Conservative Party leader.
May 2 - White House and Republican leaders in Congress reach agreement on a plan to balance the U.S. federal budget by 2002.
May 4 - The FBI says mechanical failure was the most likely cause of the crash of TWA flight 800 last July.
May 5 - Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak met in Cairo to discuss the troubled Middle East peace process.
May 5 - Report on the Busang gold find in Indonesia says claims of its potential were falsified on a scale "without precedent in mining history".
May 6 - Britain's new finance minister Gordon Brown gives the Bank of England operational responsibility for setting interest rates.
May 6 - Taiwan establishes diplomatic ties with Sao Tome and Principe.
May 7 - A U.S. study criticises both the Swiss and American governments of the time for their handling of Nazi gold after World War Two.
May 8 - Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi defies a U.N. flight ban and arrives in a Libyan plane in the capital of the impoverished West African country of Niger.
May 9 - Italian police storm the bell tower in St Mark's Square in Venice and arrest eight separatists who occupied it in a protest that put concern about secession back on Italy's political agenda.
May 9 - The first U.S. ambassador to Hanoi, former Vietnam War fighter pilot and prisoner of war Douglas "Pete" Peterson, arrives to take up his post.
May 10 - At least 1,560 people are killed and more than 2,800 are injured when an earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale strikes rural areas of eastern Iran.
May 10 - The Palestine International Bank (PIB) opens for business promising improved computerised banking services to Palestinians in the West Bank and overseas customers.
May 11 - Pope John Paul ends 32-hour visit to Lebanon with a plea for peace in the Middle East and a fully independent, democratic Lebanon.
May 11 - Garry Kasparov loses a chess match against the computer Deep Blue, the first time a machine has beaten a reigning world champion. He lost 2-1 with three draws over nine days.
May 12 - India and Pakistan agree to release each other's nationals held in prison and to set up a telephone hotline to ease tensions.
May 12 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov sign a peace accord promising to end 400 years of intermittent conflict.
May 12 - British drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan announce they are to merge, creating the world's biggest spirits and wine company.
May 13 - Japan fires its ambassador to Peru over security lapses that allowed rebel to storm his residence and take hundreds of people hostage.
May 13 - The Airports Authority of India blames Kazakh Airlines for the world's worst mid-air collision. A Kazakh aircraft collided with a Saudi Arabia Airlines Boeing 747 last November, killing 349.
May 13 - The United States and Russia agree to increase defence cooperation in areas ranging from nuclear arms destruction to military reforms.
May 14 - Turkish troops, backed by tanks and heavy artillery, push across the border into northern Iraq to attack Kurdish PKK positions.
May 16 - China and France issue a pledge on political and economic partnership as part of a visit to Beijing by President Jacques Chirac.
May 16 - The IAEA agrees to adopt a tougher, more intrusive system of inspections to ward off attempts by countries to secretly build nuclear weapons.

May 16 - British Prime Minister Tony Blair offers talks between British officials and Sinn Fein without demanding a formal IRA ceasefire first. Sinn Fein accepts the offer on May 17 but rules out a new IRA truce.
May 16 - The U.S. space shuttle Atlantis docks with the Russian Mir space station. It returns to Earth on May 24, leaving British-born astronaut Michael Foale on Mir.

May 16 - Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko leaves Kinshasa and says he is giving up executive powers but keeping the title of president. Later, Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Mahele Lieko Bokungu are killed.
May 16 - Ministers from North and South American states agree to launch talks in 1998 aimed at setting up a Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA).
May 16 - Albanian President Sali Berisha calls early elections for June 29 but most political parties still threaten to boycott the poll.
May 17 - South Korean President Kim Young-sam's son, Kim Hyun-chul, is arrested on charges of taking bribes worth millions of dollars and evading taxes.
May 17 - Laurent Kabila says he has taken power as head of state in Zaire. His forces take control of the capital Kinshasa. Kabila also renames the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
May 18 - Tajikistan's government and Islamist opposition sign a protocol on legalising political parties, part of a wider peace deal after a four-year civil war.
May 19 - Mutineers take Fayab province in Afghanistan from the control of northern Afghan leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
May 19 - A huge cyclone strikes Bangladesh killing at least 105 and damaging 400,000 houses. More than one million are made homeless.
May 20 - Laurent Kabila flies into Kinshasa from his rebel headquarters at Lubumbashi, near the border with Zambia.
May 21 - Ukraine President Leonid Kuchma and Polish President Alexander Kwasniewski sign a Declaration on Accord and Unity aimed at ending conflict and mistrust between their countries.
May 22 - President Boris Yeltsin sacks Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and the head of the general staff, Viktor Samsonov.

May 23 - At least 124 people are killed as a result of rioting in Banjarmasin, the capital of Indonesia's South Kalimantan province, after campaigning for general elections deteriorated into widespread violence.

May 23 - Ousted Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko arrives in Morocco after several days stay in Togo. In Kinshasa, Laurent Kabila presents his new government which sparks off protests between the former rebels and the political opposition.
May 23 - Russia and Belarus sign a union charter to protect political freedoms and market reforms.

May 24 - The Taleban enter the main northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif in Afghanistan, the former stronghold of General Abdul Rashid Dostum. On May 25, Dostum arrives in Turkey. On May 28, Taleban forces are reported to have been driven out of Mazar-i-Sharif.
May 25 - Pakistan becomes the first country to recognise the Taleban Islamic movement's government in Afghanistan.
May 25 - Soldiers of Sierra Leone's army oust the civilian government and President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah flees. On the 26th army major Johnny Paul Koromah declares himself head of state.

May 25 - The left-wing opposition out votes the ruling centre-right coalition in the first round of French parliamentary elections. Prime Minister Alain Juppe says on the 26th that he will resign after the June 1 second round whatever the result.
May 25 - Polish voters narrowly approve a new constitution in a referendum.
May 26 - Red Cross officials from North and South Korea sign an agreement under which the South will supply 50,000 tonnes of food aid to its hungry Northern neighbour.
May 26 - A flotilla of Chinese nationalists bent on defying Tokyo's claim to an East China Sea archipelago are thwarted by scores of Japanese patrol boats.
May 26 - Australian Prime Minister John Howard makes an apology to thousands of Aborigines taken from their parents under a past policy of forced assimilation.
May 27 - Russia and NATO sign the "Founding Act on Mutual Cooperation" in Paris and President Boris Yeltsin says Russia will no longer target nuclear missiles at NATO states.
May 27 - Tornado flattens the town of Jarrell, Texas, killing at least 27.

May 27 - Summit between Egypt and Israel to revive the Middle East peace process ends without breakthroughs, but gives hope further talks will help overcome differences over Jewish settlement of Arab land.
May 27 - U.S. Supreme Court says the Paula Jones sexual harassment case against President Bill Clinton can go ahead, rather than wait for him to leave office.
May 28 - Ukraine agrees to allow Russia to keep its share of the ex-Soviet Black Sea Fleet at Sevastopol for the next 20 years.
May 28 - Ninety-three Vietnamese boatpeople arrive in Hanoi on the last U.N. chartered repatriation flight from Hong Kong.
May 28 - Three suspected urban guerrillas shoot dead Greek ship owner Constantine Peratikos.
May 29 - NATO initials a pact with Ukraine marking a further stage in the redrawing of the security map of Europe.
May 29 - Singapore court awards Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and other party colleagues Singapore $8.08 (US$5.65) million after an opponent called them liars.
May 29 - Laurent Kabila is sworn in as president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and promises elections in April 1999.
May 29 - British Prime Minister Tony Blair and U.S. President Bill Clinton cement their warm personal relations by declaring themselves political twins from a new generation.
May 29 - General election in Indonesia sweeps the ruling Golkar party to victory with 74 percent of the vote.

May 30 - U.S. marines using 15 helicopters evacuate nearly 1,000 Americans and others from Sierra Leone despite coup leaders in the West African state ordering the closure of borders and banning all flights.
May 30 - NATO states and 27 partnership countries meet for the first time in a new body created to try to meet the security worries of countries unlikely to gain alliance membership next July.

May 30 - The United States and its Western allies tell Bosnian leaders to implement the Dayton peace accords in full or face sanctions. They appoint Carlos Westerndorp to succeed Carl Bildt as the new High Representative for Bosnia from June 20.
May 31 - Ukraine President Leonid Kuchma and Russian President Boris Yeltsin sign a long-delayed friendship treaty declaring a "strategic partnership" between the two Slav states.
May 31 - Association of South East Asian States says it will admit Burma, Cambodia and Laos as members in July.

Notable deaths in May included: Narciso Yepes, Spanish classical guitarist (3rd); Wijayananda Dahanayake, former Sri Lankan prime minister (4); Kai-Uwe von Hassel, former West German defence minister (8); Marco Ferreri, Italian film director (9); Laurie Lee, British author (14); Giuseppe De Santis, Italian film director (16); Manfred von Ardenne, German inventor (26).
